title: Majestic 12

tellings.quote: So, this is like a reported committee in the in the I guess 40s and 50s and like, you know, Nathan Twining, James Forrestal, Vannevar Bush, people like that.

plain: Michels describes Majestic 12 as a reported secret committee on UFOs in the 1940s and 50s whose members included General Nathan Twining, Defense Secretary James Forrestal and the scientist Vannevar Bush. Those names come from a disputed briefing paper for president-elect Dwight Eisenhower, dated 1952, which turned up anonymously on film in 1984. It lists all three among twelve members of a group created by Truman's order of 24 September 1947, and says Forrestal's death "created a vacancy which remained unfilled until 01 August, 1950." A 1954 memo to Twining, also disputed, speaks of an "MJ-12 SSP briefing" at the White House. Whether such a committee ever met holds only as far as those papers are genuine.

discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper lists "Dr. Vannevar Bush", "Secy. James V. Forrestal" and "Gen. Nathan F. Twining" among the twelve members of a group it dates to Truman's order of 24 September 1947, and says Forrestal's death "created a vacancy which remained unfilled until 01 August, 1950", when Walter B. Smith replaced him. The names and the span into the 1950s that Michels gives are the paper's; that such a committee sat holds only as far as the paper is genuine.

A one-page memorandum dated 14 July 1954 from Robert Cutler to General Nathan Twining that Jaime Shandera and William Moore reported finding in July 1985 in Record Group 341, Entry 267, at the National Archives. The Archives says it "poses problems": the series is filed by Top Secret register number and it bears none; its marking "Top Secret Restricted Information" came into use at the National Security Council only under Nixon; it has no letterhead or watermark; the NSC minutes hold no meeting on 16 July 1954; and Cutler was abroad on 14 July 1954. Stanton Friedman judged it "almost certainly genuine", answering that Cutler had left instructions with NSC executive secretary James Lay. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds a copy marked "BOGUS" by hand. The memo, dated 14 July 1954, tells General Twining that "The President has decid[[ed]] that the [[MJ-12]] SSP br[[ief]]ing should take place during the already sched[[ul]]ed White [[Ho]]use meeting of July 16" (double brackets mark letters illegible in the FBI's copy). It would carry an MJ-12 briefing, with Twining invited, into the 1950s end of the span Michels gives; it does so only as far as the memo is genuine.
